primary_claim: Across 16 fresh NEON small-mammal sites, pooled community spatial continuity was redundant with individual-species continuity rather than emergent from species turnover.

supported.claim: No positive emergent connectivity gain occurred.
supported.evidence: 0/16 sites had community survival fraction greater than the best single species; median gain = 0.
At no site did the guild survive a canonical world that every eligible individual species failed.

supported.claim: At least one individual species survived every distinct canonical world at every fresh site.
supported.evidence: best single-species survival fraction = 1.0 at 16/16 sites.
ORNL community survival = 0.25 versus best species = 1.0; emergent gain = -0.75.

prohibited: Species turnover creates emergent spatial continuity in the consumed programme.
The species with highest node coverage is necessarily the best world-survival species.
The pattern proves species sorting, mass effects, habitat filtering or dispersal mechanism.
The result generalizes beyond the fixed NEON target-small-mammal system without new validation.
Post-response alternative tie handling may rescore or alter the consumed primary endpoint.

terminology.redundancy: community spatial world survival is already matched by one or more individual species
terminology.strict_emergence: guild survives a canonical world while all individual eligible species fail it
terminology.weakest_link_effect: pooling taxa adds positive nodes that can invalidate worlds under an all-positive support criterion
